This is a sectional view of a septic tank system.

**Title/Label:** SECTIONAL VIEW

**Labeled Components:**
- **C.I. MANHOLE:** Two manholes are indicated on either end of the tank.
- **1/4" RODS:** These rods are likely used for inspection and cleaning purposes.
- **WATER LINE:** The water line is shown running through the tank.
- **OVERFLOW:** An overflow pipe is depicted on the right side of the tank.
- **INLET:** The inlet pipe is shown on the left side of the tank.
- **SLOPE SLIGHTLY TOWARD INLET:** This indicates the direction of flow within the tank.

**Arrows:**
- There are no directional arrows explicitly pointing to specific components.

**Inputs:**
- **INLET:** Water enters the tank through this pipe.

**Outputs:**
- **OVERFLOW:** If the tank becomes full, water will flow out through this pipe.

**Technical Purpose:**
The diagram illustrates the cross-sectional view of a septic tank system. It shows how water flows into the tank through the inlet pipe, moves along the water line, and eventually exits the tank through the overflow pipe if necessary. The presence of manholes allows for maintenance and inspection of the system. The 1/4" rods are likely used for cleaning and checking the condition of the tank's interior.

regions.extracted_text: Location and Construction—The septic tank, although air-tight and supposedly water-tight, should be located as far from the house and the well or spring as convenience and local surroundings will permit. It thus reduces the danger of pollution or nuisance in case of leakage or improper operation of the system.
